description: A superintendent must approve the operating plan for a weather-related remote instruction day, including instructional access, meal access, health support, and family communication, with input from transportation, information technology, nursing, and family engagement staff.

shared_context.S1: A winter storm is expected to make normal school travel unsafe tomorrow, and the district is preparing to operate one remote instruction day.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Morgan Lee approves the final district operating plan.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan schedules instruction through the learning management system beginning at 8:00 a.m., sends meals by regular bus routes, directs health questions to the usual school voicemail, and assumes families can use digital materials.
shared_context.S4: The district's morning operations briefing routinely includes transportation, information technology, nursing, and family engagement reports before the superintendent signs a weather-related operating plan.

PF1.text: The transportation department's storm route review found that no buses can safely travel tomorrow; meals can instead be made available for on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Ms. Shah completed the route review this afternoon, but the results have not yet been added to the operations briefing packet.

PF2.text: District learning-management-system authentication will be offline for scheduled maintenance from 8:00 to 11:00 a.m. tomorrow. Mr. Brooks confirmed the maintenance window with the vendor today, but the vendor notice has not yet been attached to the remote-day draft. Instructional files must be distributed by email as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing by 7:30 a.m.

PF3.text: The district nurse coverage plan requires a staffed nurse hotline from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. tomorrow for students who need medication or urgent health guidance during remote instruction. Nurse Ruiz confirmed the coverage roster this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the plan.

PF4.text: Family outreach confirmations show that 38 households lack reliable internet access, and those households need printed learning packets plus bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali. Ms. Green completed the confirmations this week, but the family-access summary is still being compiled and is not in the draft.

acceptance_conditions: The district must operate a remote instruction day.
Instructional materials must be distributed as downloadable PDFs and made available for printing.
Materials must be available by 7:30 a.m.
Meals must be offered by on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
A staffed nurse hotline must operate from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.
The family-access plan must provide printed packets and bilingual phone check-ins in Spanish and Somali.
The plan must contain formal commitments for technology distribution, meal pickup, nurse coverage, and family outreach.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'technology_distribution' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'meal_pickup' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'nurse_hotline' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'family_outreach' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The route review changes meal access from regular bus delivery to on-site pickup at North Campus and South Campus from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
The maintenance window changes instructional delivery to downloadable PDFs and printable packets and requires release by exactly 7:30 a.m. plus a technology-distribution commitment.
The coverage plan changes health support from the usual voicemail to a staffed nurse hotline operating exactly from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and requires a nurse-hotline commitment.
The family confirmations change access from digital-only materials to printed packets and bilingual phone check-ins in exactly Spanish and Somali and require a family-outreach commitment.
